title: Exothermic and endothermic: how hot packs and cold packs work
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What is the difference between exothermic and endothermic?
How does an instant ice pack get cold?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Heat flows out of hot packs and into cold packs

explain.say: Every chemical reaction either gives out energy or takes it in. Hot packs and instant cold packs use one of each.

draw.text: Exothermic and endothermic: how hot packs and cold packs work

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Heat flows out of hot packs and into cold packs

explain.say: A hot pack uses an exothermic change, such as iron rusting or a liquid crystallising. It releases heat into its surroundings, so it feels warm.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Heat flows out of hot packs and into cold packs

explain.say: An instant cold pack uses an endothermic change. Squeezing it bursts an inner pouch of water, and a solid such as ammonium nitrate dissolves, taking in heat.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Heat flows out of hot packs and into cold packs

explain.say: The energy to pull the solid apart is taken from the water and from your skin, so the pack can drop close to freezing, which is handy for a sports injury.

faq.a: An exothermic reaction gives out energy, usually as heat, so its surroundings get warmer. Burning, rusting and hand warmers are examples.
An endothermic change takes in energy from its surroundings, so they get colder. Instant cold packs and baking soda reacting with vinegar are examples.

faq.q: How does an instant cold pack work?
faq.a: Squeezing it breaks a pouch of water inside. A solid like ammonium nitrate or urea dissolves in the water, and that dissolving takes in heat, so the pack turns cold.
asks: How does an ice pack get cold without a freezer?

faq.q: Where does the heat go in a cold pack?
faq.a: It is used to break apart the solid crystals as they dissolve. That energy comes from the water and from anything touching the pack, like your skin.
asks: Why does a cold pack feel cold?

faq.a: Yes. All burning is exothermic, giving out energy as heat and light, which is why we use fuels for warmth and cooking.
asks: Does fire give out or take in heat?

facts: Dissolving ammonium nitrate in water takes in heat, which is why it is used in instant cold packs.
All burning is exothermic, releasing energy as heat and light.

quiz.say: An instant cold pack feels cold because the change inside is what?
quiz.show: An instant cold pack feels cold because the change inside is what?
quiz.why: The dissolving solid takes in heat from the water and your skin, so the pack feels cold.

wrong.0: An exothermic change would make the pack warm, like a hand warmer.
wrong.1: No ice forms; the pack gets cold because heat is taken in.
